mainTopic: Selling land by size: what a plain 'בית כור' means, how extra land is paid for, and when a nine-קבין surplus must be returned
overview: The גמרא first asks what a plain sale of 'a בית כור' of land means when the seller adds no extra words. The two halves of the משנה point in opposite directions, so nothing can be learned from it. A ברייתא then seems to treat a plain sale like 'more or less,' and רב אשי's point about the repeated words 'I am selling you' proves that reading. Next the גמרא asks why the משנה protects only the seller, who may choose between taking money or land back for extra land. It answers that the buyer is protected through the price: he always pays the lower one, today's price if land got cheaper and the original price if it got more expensive. Finally, רב הונא and רב נחמן argue about the משנה's nine-קבין rule. רב הונא says a nine-קבין surplus always goes back as land, even in a huge valley. רב נחמן says the allowed extra is a ratio of seven and a half קבין per כור.

steps.title: Proof from the first half of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to prove from the first case of the משנה that a plain sale is like 'more or less.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If the seller promised an exact rope measurement and gave even a tiny bit less, he must take it off the price. If he gave even a tiny bit more, the buyer must give it back. This implies that without these words, a plain sale counts as 'more or less.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the first case of the משנה closely and draws a hidden lesson from it. It argues that a plain sale must be like 'more or less.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives the strict rule (every tiny difference counts) only when the seller said 'measured with a rope' (מדה בחבל). The גמרא reasons that if a plain sale were already strict, the משנה would not need that phrase. So a plain sale must be the lenient kind, like הן חסר הן יתר.

keyTerms.meaning: less by even the smallest amount
he must deduct it from the price
he must give it back
plain, without any extra words
'whether less or more,' a sale that allows some difference
is like, is treated the same as

phrases.english: If it is even slightly less, he must deduct;
if it is even slightly more, he must return it.
This implies that a plain sale, without further words,
is like 'more or less'!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא סְתָמָא כְּ״הֵן חָסֵר הֵן יָתֵר״ דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the question about a plain sale by bringing a first proof from the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: A plain sale of a בית כור is treated like הן חסר הן יתר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The first case of the משנה, which gives the strict rule only when the seller said 'with a rope.'

steps.title: The second half of the משנה implies the opposite
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the second case of the משנה can be read to prove exactly the opposite.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now read the end of the משנה: if he said 'more or less,' then even a quarter-קב per סאה less or more is fine, and the buyer keeps it. This implies that a plain sale is like an exact rope measurement!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof by reading the second half of the משנה the same careful way. This time the result points in the opposite direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives the lenient rule only when the seller said הן חסר הן יתר. Using the same reasoning as before, a plain sale must then be strict, like מדה בחבל. So the same משנה supports both sides.

keyTerms.meaning: say (read) the end part of the source
a quarter-קַב for every סְאָה, a small set margin
it is his; the sale stands
measured with a rope, an exact measurement

phrases.english: Say the latter part:

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אָמַר לוֹ: ״הֵן חָסֵר הֵן יָתֵר״;
phrases.english: And if he said to him: 'More or less,'
even if he gave a quarter per se'a less
phrases.notes: A quarter-קב for each סאה. A סאה has six קבין, so this is about one twenty-fourth.

phrases.english: or gave a quarter per se'a more, it is his.
This implies that a plain sale
is like measuring with a rope!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Cancels out the proof of step 1 by drawing the opposite lesson from the same משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the משנה as proof for either side.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The inference from the first case is balanced by an equally strong opposite inference from the second case.

steps.title: Nothing can be learned from this משנה
steps.stepSummary: Since the משנה points both ways, the גמרא drops it as a source.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, nothing can be learned from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes this first attempt. The משנה cannot settle the question, so the גמרא will look for another source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each half of the משנה gives a clear rule only for the case it names. The plain case is left in between, so the משנה tells us nothing about it.

keyTerms.meaning: there is nothing to learn from it

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה only rules on 'with a rope' and 'more or less.' It does not rule on the plain sale; a ברייתא in steps 4-7 settles that.

phrases.english: Rather, from this nothing can be learned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the result of steps 1 and 2: the משנה is not usable as proof.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה gives no answer about a plain sale.

steps.title: Proof from a ברייתא listing three phrasings
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists a plain 'בית כור' alongside 'about a בית כור' and 'more or less,' and gives all of them the lenient rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'I sell you a בית כור of land'; 'I sell you about a בית כור of land'; 'I sell you more or less.' Even if it was a quarter-קב per סאה less or more, it is his. So a plain sale is also like 'more or less'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source, a ברייתא. It seems to state openly that a plain sale gets the same lenient rule as 'more or less.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists three sentences, and the first one is just 'a בית כור' with no extra words. All three end with the same lenient ruling. So a plain sale looks like it is treated as הן חסר הן יתר.

keyTerms.meaning: a field large enough to plant a כּוֹר of seed
about a בֵּית כּוֹר, roughly that size
apparently, this shows that

phrases.english: Come and hear:
'I am selling you a beit kor of earth';
'I am selling you about a beit kor of earth';

phrases.aramaic: ״הֵן חָסֵר הֵן יָתֵר אֲנִי מוֹכֵר לָךְ״ –
phrases.english: 'I am selling you more or less' –
even if he gave a quarter per se'a less,
or gave a quarter per se'a more, it is his.
Apparently, a plain sale too
is like 'more or less'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the משנה failed, a new source is brought.
steps.raayaObject: A plain sale is treated like הן חסר הן יתר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא that gives the plain 'בית כור' sale the same lenient rule as 'more or less.'

steps.title: The ברייתא is one explanation, not three cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the ברייתא as one sentence explaining itself, so the plain case only gets leniency when 'more or less' was said.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the ברייתא is explaining itself: when is 'a בית כור' treated as 'about a בית כור'? When he told him, 'more or less.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the proof away. It says the three phrases are not three separate cases but one case explained step by step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading, 'a בית כור' becomes 'about a בית כור' only when the seller added הן חסר הן יתר. So the ברייתא never gives the lenient rule to a truly plain sale. The proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: there, in that source
it is explaining itself
for example, such as when

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the three phrases as three separate sales here. In this step the גמרא claims they are all ONE sale, with each phrase explaining the one before it.

phrases.english: There, it is explaining itself:

phrases.aramaic: אֵיזֶהוּ בֵּית כּוֹר שֶׁהִיא כְּבֵית כּוֹר?
phrases.english: Which beit kor counts as 'about a beit kor'?

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ: ״הֵן חָסֵר הֵן יָתֵר״.
phrases.english: Where he said to him: 'More or less.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 4 by re-reading the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the ברייתא as proof about a plain sale.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the three phrases are separate cases, but they may be one case explained.

steps.title: רב אשי: why repeat 'I am selling you'?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי argues that the repeated words 'I am selling you' show these are separate sales.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי objected: If so, why do I need 'I am selling you,' 'I am selling you' again and again?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks the answer of step 5. He points to the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא were one sentence explaining itself, it would not repeat 'I am selling you' in each phrase. The repetition shows each phrase is its own sale. So the plain 'בית כור' is a separate case that gets the lenient rule.

keyTerms.meaning: he challenged it
if so
why do I need it?

phrases.english: Rav Ashi objected to this:

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, ״אֲנִי מוֹכֵר לָךְ״ ״אֲנִי מוֹכֵר לָךְ״ לְמָה לִי?
phrases.english: If so, why do I need 'I am selling you,' 'I am selling you'?

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא is one case explaining itself.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The repeated words 'I am selling you' only make sense if each phrase is a separate sale.

steps.title: Conclusion: a plain sale is like 'more or less'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts רב אשי's point and concludes that a plain sale is like הן חסר הן יתר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, must we not learn from this that a plain sale is also like 'more or less'? Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי states the conclusion his question leads to, and the גמרא agrees. The question is settled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the three phrases are separate sales, the plain 'בית כור' sale has its own lenient ruling. So a seller who said only 'a בית כור' may be off by up to a quarter-קב per סאה.

keyTerms.meaning: rather, is it not so that
learn from it; yes, that is the conclusion

steps.whatToRemember: A plain sale of 'a בית כור' is treated like הן חסר הן יתר. A small difference, up to a quarter-קב per סאה, does not change the deal.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the default rule for land sold by size when the seller adds no extra words.

phrases.english: Rather, must we not learn from it

phrases.aramaic: סְתָמָא נָמֵי כְּ״הֵן חָסֵר הֵן יָתֵר״ דָּמֵי?
phrases.english: that a plain sale too is like 'more or less'?
Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the result of רב אשי's challenge, bringing back the proof of step 4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A plain sale of a בית כור is treated like הן חסר הן יתר.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: The buyer pays money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line of the משנה that says the buyer returns money for the extra land.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: What does he return to him? Money, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה so it can discuss it. This is a setup for the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught that a buyer who got too much land pays the seller money for the extra. It added that the חכמים set it up this way 'to strengthen the seller's position', so the seller can choose between taking the land back or taking money. The next step questions this reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Money, coins
Returns, gives back
Etc.: the rest of the quote is assumed

phrases.english: What does he return to him?
phrases.notes: This is the buyer, who got more land than he paid for, giving something back to the seller.

phrases.english: Money, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' points to the rest of the משנה line: the חכמים gave this rule to strengthen the seller's position.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה after the discussion of the plain sale ended in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A buyer who received extra land pays the seller money for it, a rule made to strengthen the seller's position.

steps.title: Is only the seller protected? A ברייתא protects the buyer too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether only the seller is protected, and brings a ברייתא where the court forces the seller to sell extra land to the buyer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we really say to strengthen the seller's position but not the buyer's? A ברייתא teaches: if the seller gave 7½ קבין per כור less, or 7½ קבין per כור more, it is the buyer's. If the difference is more than that, we force the seller to sell and the buyer to buy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's reason, 'to strengthen the seller's position.' It brings a ברייתא where the seller is forced to sell, which seems to strengthen the buyer's position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה seems to say only the seller gets a choice. But the ברייתא says 'we force the seller to sell', which sounds like the buyer can make the seller sell him the extra land for money. So the buyer seems to be protected too, and that clashes with the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: To strengthen his position, to give him the advantage
Seller
Buyer
It reached him: it is his, no adjustment is needed
We force (the court forces)

steps.confusionAlert: 7½ קבין per כור is the same amount as the משנה's 'quarter-קב per סאה' (a כור has 30 סאה). It is the same small margin, just counted per כור.

phrases.english: To strengthen the seller's position, we say,

phrases.aramaic: לְיַפּוֹת כֹּחוֹ שֶׁל לוֹקֵחַ לָא אָמְרִינַן?!
phrases.english: but to strengthen the buyer's position, we do not say?!
But it was taught in a ברייתא:
If he gave seven and a half kav per kor less,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ הוֹתִיר שִׁבְעַת קַבִּין וּמֶחֱצָה לְכוֹר –
phrases.english: or gave seven and a half kav per kor more,
it is his.
More than this,
we force the seller to sell
and the buyer to buy.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְיַפּוֹת כֹּחוֹ שֶׁל מוֹכֵר אָמְרִינַן, לְיַפּוֹת כֹּחוֹ שֶׁל לוֹקֵחַ לָא אָמְרִינַן?! וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in the משנה line quoted in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's reason that the rule is meant to strengthen the seller's position.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא forces the seller to sell extra land, which seems to strengthen the buyer's position as well.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about land that got cheaper
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא speaks about land that was expensive at the sale and is cheap now, so the seller must take today's lower price.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the case is where land was expensive at first and is cheap now. We tell the seller: If you want to give me land and take money, charge me today's cheap price.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא does not let the buyer force a sale. It only covers the price when land got cheaper.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seller still chooses whether to take money or land, so the משנה stands. But if he chooses money, he cannot charge the old high price. The ברייתא's 'we force the seller to sell' means he must sell at today's lower price.

keyTerms.meaning: Expensive
Cheap, a low price
At first, originally (at the time of the sale)
Now

phrases.english: There, it is a case where it was expensive at first,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the ברייתא from the last step. 'It' is the land's price.

phrases.english: and is cheap now;
where we say to him:
phrases.notes: We say this to the seller, speaking for the buyer.

phrases.english: If you are giving me land,
give it to me at the cheap price of now.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם, כְּגוֹן דַּהֲוָה יַקִּירָא מֵעִיקָּרָא, וְזָל הַשְׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9 by limiting the ברייתא to a specific price situation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the ברייתא is about a drop in price.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא means the buyer can force the seller to sell him the extra land.
steps.terutzMaskana: The seller still chooses, but if he takes money when prices have dropped, he must accept today's lower price.

steps.title: Another ברייתא: pay the original price
steps.stepSummary: A different ברייתא says the buyer pays by the price at the original sale, not today's price.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: When he pays him, he pays at the price he bought it from him for!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 10 with another ברייתא that says the buyer pays the original price.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 said the buyer pays today's price. This ברייתא says he pays the price from the time of the sale. The two rules seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Market price, rate
When he gives (pays) him

phrases.english: But it was taught in a ברייתא:
When he gives him,
phrases.notes: The buyer paying the seller money for the extra land.

phrases.english: he gives him according to the price at which he bought from him!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: כְּשֶׁהוּא נוֹתֵן לוֹ – נוֹתֵן לוֹ כְּשַׁעַר שֶׁלָּקַח מִמֶּנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 10, which set the payment at today's price.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 10 that the buyer pays at today's price.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says the payment follows the original sale price.

steps.title: That ברייתא is about land that got more expensive
steps.stepSummary: The second ברייתא speaks about land that was cheap at the sale and is expensive now, so the buyer pays the old lower price.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the case is where land was cheap at first and has become expensive now.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the second ברייתא is about rising prices, so both ברייתות fit together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If prices went down, the buyer pays today's price (step 10). If prices went up, he pays the original price (this step). Either way the buyer pays the lower price, and that is how the buyer's position is also protected.

keyTerms.meaning: Became expensive

steps.whatToRemember: The seller chooses between money and land, but if he takes money, the buyer always pays the lower price: today's price if land got cheaper, the original price if it got more expensive.

phrases.english: There, it is a case where it was cheap at first,
and it has become expensive now.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם, כְּגוֹן דַּהֲוָה זוּלָא מֵעִיקָּרָא, וְיָקְרָא לַהּ הַשְׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 11 by limiting the second ברייתא to a rise in price.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): each ברייתא covers a different price change.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות disagree about which price the buyer pays.
steps.terutzMaskana: When prices rise, the buyer pays the original lower price; when they fall, he pays today's lower price.

steps.title: Quoting the nine-קבין line of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: if the extra land in a field is a plot that takes nine קבין of seed, the special rule applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'For if he left in the field an area of nine קבין, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה to set up the discussion that comes next. The line is about extra land big enough to sow nine קבין of seed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that a plot of nine קבין in a field counts as a real, usable piece of land. So the buyer gives back the land itself, not money. The 'etc.' points to the rest of that line, which also mentions a garden. The אמוראים are about to argue over how far this rule reaches.

keyTerms.meaning: Left over, the extra land beyond what was sold
An area that takes nine קבין of seed to sow
A measure of seed; a field's size is described by how much seed it takes

phrases.english: For if he left over in the field
phrases.notes: The 'he' is the seller. The field he handed over came out bigger than he promised.

phrases.english: an area of nine kav, etc.
phrases.notes: 'Etc.' means the גמרא is pointing to the rest of the משנה line, which also mentions a garden.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁאִם שִׁיֵּיר בַּשָּׂדֶה בֵּית תִּשְׁעָה קַבִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the discussion of which price to use (Steps 8-12) to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A nine-קבין plot of extra land in a field is returned as land, not paid for in money.

steps.title: רב הונא: the nine-קבין rule applies even in a huge valley
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says the משנה's nine-קבין rule applies even when the field sold is a very large valley.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: The nine קבין that the חכמים spoke of apply even in a large valley.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא explains how far the משנה's nine-קבין rule reaches. He says it applies even in a very large field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a huge valley, nine קבין is only a tiny part of the whole field. You might think it is too small to matter there. רב הונא says no: a nine-קבין plot is a real field on its own, so it is returned as land even in a big valley. This holds even if the extra is smaller than the normal allowed ratio.

keyTerms.meaning: A large valley, meaning a very big field
'That they said', referring to the חכמים of the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב הונא means that nine קבין is a fixed limit only for small fields. His whole point is that the size of the field does not matter. Nine קבין always counts as real land.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
The nine kav that they spoke of
apply even in a large valley.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: תִּשְׁעָה קַבִּין שֶׁאָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how far the משנה line quoted in Step 13 reaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A nine-קבין surplus is always returned as land, no matter how large the whole field is.

steps.title: רב נחמן: the allowed extra grows with the field's size
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן disagrees with רב הונא. He says the allowed extra is seven and a half קבין for every כור of field.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן said: He allows seven and a half קבין for each and every כור.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives an opposing view. He says the allowed extra is measured by ratio: seven and a half קבין for every כור in the field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כור is thirty סאה. A quarter-קב for each סאה comes to seven and a half קבין per כור. So in a big field of several כור, the seller's allowed extra can be more than nine קבין. The buyer does not have to give it back. This is the opposite of רב הונא, who says nine קבין always goes back.

keyTerms.meaning: A large field measure, equal to thirty סאה
A field measure equal to six קבין
Half

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא: nine קבין always counts as real land, even in a huge field. רב נחמן: the allowed extra is a ratio, seven and a half קבין per כור, so big fields allow more.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up two different ways to read the משנה: a fixed size that always matters, or a ratio that grows with the field.

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman said:
He allows seven and a half kav
phrases.notes: That is a quarter-קב for each סאה. A כור has thirty סאה, so thirty quarter-קבין make seven and a half.

phrases.english: for each and every kor.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: נוֹתֵן שִׁבְעַת קַבִּין וּמֶחֱצָה לְכׇל כּוֹר וָכוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב הונא from Step 14 about large fields.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The allowed extra is figured by ratio: seven and a half קבין per כור. In a large field, extra within that ratio stays with the buyer even if it is more than nine קבין.
